(سُورَةُ الحُجُراتِ ثَمانِيَ عَشْرَةَ آيَةً مَدَنِيَّةٌ)
(بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ)

(p-104) ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَرْفَعُوا أصْواتَكم فَوْقَ صَوْتِ النَّبِيِّ ولا تَجْهَرُوا لَهُ بِالقَوْلِ كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكم لِبَعْضٍ أنْ تَحْبَطَ أعْمالُكم وأنْتُمْ لا تَشْعُرُونَ﴾ ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أصْواتَهم عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ امْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهم لِلتَّقْوى لَهم مَغْفِرَةٌ وأجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يُنادُونَكَ مِن وراءِ الحُجُراتِ أكْثَرُهم لا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ ﴿ولَوْ أنَّهم صَبَرُوا حَتّى تَخْرُجَ إلَيْهِمْ لَكانَ خَيْرًا لَهم واللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إنْ جاءَكم فاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوا أنْ تُصِيبُوا قَوْمًا بِجَهالَةٍ فَتُصْبِحُوا عَلى ما فَعَلْتُمْ نادِمِينَ﴾ [الحجرات: 6] ﴿واعْلَمُوا أنَّ فِيكم رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لَوْ يُطِيعُكم في كَثِيرٍ مِنَ الأمْرِ لَعَنِتُّمْ ولَكِنَّ اللَّهَ حَبَّبَ إلَيْكُمُ الإيمانَ وزَيَّنَهُ في قُلُوبِكم وكَرَّهَ إلَيْكُمُ الكُفْرَ والفُسُوقَ والعِصْيانَ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الرّاشِدُونَ﴾ [الحجرات: 7] ﴿فَضْلًا مِنَ اللَّهِ ونِعْمَةً واللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ [الحجرات: 8] ﴿وإنْ طائِفَتانِ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا فَأصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُما فَإنْ بَغَتْ إحْداهُما عَلى الأُخْرى فَقاتِلُوا الَّتِي تَبْغِي حَتّى تَفِيءَ إلى أمْرِ اللَّهِ فَإنْ فاءَتْ فَأصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُما بِالعَدْلِ وأقْسِطُوا إنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ المُقْسِطِينَ﴾ [الحجرات: 9] ﴿إنَّما المُؤْمِنُونَ إخْوَةٌ فَأصْلِحُوا بَيْنَ أخَوَيْكم واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكم تُرْحَمُونَ﴾ [الحجرات: 10] ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِن قَوْمٍ عَسى أنْ يَكُونُوا خَيْرًا مِنهم ولا نِساءٌ مِن نِساءٍ عَسى أنْ يَكُنَّ خَيْرًا مِنهُنَّ ولا تَلْمِزُوا أنْفُسَكم ولا تَنابَزُوا بِالألْقابِ بِئْسَ الِاسْمُ الفُسُوقُ بَعْدَ الإيمانِ ومَن لَمْ يَتُبْ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الظّالِمُونَ﴾ [الحجرات: 11] ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيرًا مِنَ الظَّنِّ إنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إثْمٌ ولا تَجَسَّسُوا ولا يَغْتَبْ بَعْضُكم بَعْضًا أيُحِبُّ أحَدُكم أنْ يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أخِيهِ مَيْتًا فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إنَّ اللَّهَ تَوّابٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [الحجرات: 12] ﴿يا أيُّها النّاسُ إنّا خَلَقْناكم مِن ذَكَرٍ وأُنْثى وجَعَلْناكم شُعُوبًا وقَبائِلَ لِتَعارَفُوا إنَّ أكْرَمَكم عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أتْقاكم إنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ﴾ [الحجرات: 13] ﴿قالَتِ الأعْرابُ آمَنّا قُلْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا ولَكِنْ قُولُوا أسْلَمْنا ولَمّا يَدْخُلِ الإيمانُ في قُلُوبِكم وإنْ تُطِيعُوا اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ لا يَلِتْكم مِن أعْمالِكم شَيْئًا إنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [الحجرات: 14] ﴿إنَّما المُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَرْتابُوا وجاهَدُوا بِأمْوالِهِمْ وأنْفُسِهِمْ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الصّادِقُونَ﴾ [الحجرات: 15] ﴿قُلْ أتُعَلِّمُونَ اللَّهَ بِدِينِكم واللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ واللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ [الحجرات: 16] ﴿يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ أنْ أسْلَمُوا قُلْ لا تَمُنُّوا عَلَيَّ إسْلامَكم بَلِ اللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيْكم أنْ هَداكم لِلْإيمانِ إنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ﴾ [الحجرات: 17] ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ واللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [الحجرات: 18]

At-tanabuz bil-alqab (mutual nicknaming): calling one another by it; it is of the form tafa'ala from nabazahu. The Banu Fulan yatanabazuna and yatanazabuna. It is said: an-nabz and an-nazb are the bad nickname.

Al-laqab (nickname) is what a person is called by, other than his given name or his kunyah (teknonym). It is of two kinds: ugly, which is what a person dislikes because it belittles him and is a reproach; and good, which is the opposite, such as as-Siddiq for Abu Bakr, al-Faruq for Umar, and Asad Allah (Lion of God) for Hamzah, may Allah be pleased with them.

Tajassasa al-amr: he sought it out and searched for its hidden aspects. It is from the root jass, and from it comes al-jasus (spy), who searches for the faults in order to know them. The senses of a person are called al-hawass, with ha' and jim.

Ash-sha'b (nation): the first of the six levels into which the Arabs were divided, namely: ash-sha'b, al-qabilah (tribe), al-'imarah (clan), al-batn (sub-clan), al-fakhdh (branch), and al-fasilah (subdivision). Thus ash-sha'b includes the qaba'il, the qabilah includes the 'amā'ir, the 'imarah includes the butun, the batn includes the afkhadh, and the fakhdh includes the fasa'il. Khuzaymah is a sha'b, Kinanah is a qabilah, Quraysh is an 'imarah, Qusayy is a batn, Hashim is a fakhdh, and al-Abbas is a fasilah. The term shu'ub was so named because the tribes branched out (tasha''abat) from them. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "ash-shu'ub" means the butun (sub-clans). This is other than what the lexicographers have agreed upon, and a disagreement on this will come up at His words: ﴿وجَعَلْناكم شُعُوبًا﴾ [49:13].

Al-qabilah is below ash-sha'b; it is likened to the qaba'il of the head (the sutures of the skull), because they are pieces that face one another.

Alta yaaltu: with damm and kasr of the lam, alta (also), and lata yalitu and alata yaliitu (quadriliteral): three dialects transmitted by Abu 'Ubaydah, and the meaning is "he fell short." Ru'bah said:

"And a night full of dew I travelled, and the lion did not hold me back from its journey."

That is: it did not prevent me nor restrain me. Al-Hutay'ah said:

"Convey to the nobles of Banu Sa'd, with the utmost effort of the message, without shortfall or lie."

(p-105) ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ ﴿ياأيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَرْفَعُوا أصْواتَكم فَوْقَ صَوْتِ النَّبِيِّ ولا تَجْهَرُوا لَهُ بِالقَوْلِ كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكم لِبَعْضٍ أنْ تَحْبَطَ أعْمالُكم وأنْتُمْ لا تَشْعُرُونَ﴾ ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أصْواتَهم عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ امْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهم لِلتَّقْوى لَهم مَغْفِرَةٌ وأجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يُنادُونَكَ مِن وراءِ الحُجُراتِ أكْثَرُهم لا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ ﴿ولَوْ أنَّهم صَبَرُوا حَتّى تَخْرُجَ إلَيْهِمْ لَكانَ خَيْرًا لَهم واللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ ﴿ياأيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إنْ جاءَكم فاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوا أنْ تُصِيبُوا قَوْمًا بِجَهالَةٍ فَتُصْبِحُوا عَلى ما فَعَلْتُمْ نادِمِينَ﴾ [الحجرات: 6] ﴿واعْلَمُوا أنَّ فِيكم رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لَوْ يُطِيعُكم في كَثِيرٍ مِنَ الأمْرِ لَعَنِتُّمْ ولَكِنَّ اللَّهَ حَبَّبَ إلَيْكُمُ الإيمانَ وزَيَّنَهُ في قُلُوبِكم وكَرَّهَ إلَيْكُمُ الكُفْرَ والفُسُوقَ والعِصْيانَ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الرّاشِدُونَ﴾ [الحجرات: 7] ﴿فَضْلًا مِنَ اللَّهِ ونِعْمَةً واللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ [الحجرات: 8].

This surah is Medinan. Its connection with what precedes it is evident, because He mentioned the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions, then said: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [48:29]. So perhaps some of the believers who do righteous deeds did something that ought to be forbidden, and so the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, do not put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾.

It was the custom of the Arabs, and it remains so to this day, to share opinions, for each to speak as he wishes and do what he loves. Some of those who had not trained themselves in the etiquette of the Sharia did some of this. Qatadah said: "Some people would say: it should be such-and-such if such-and-such were revealed." Al-Hasan said: "A people slaughtered sacrifices before the Prophet (ﷺ), and a people did something on their own opinion during one of his campaigns, so this verse was revealed forbidding all of that." Ibn 'Abbas said: "They were forbidden to speak before his speech." The Arabs say: "I went ahead (taqaddamtu) in such-and-such," and "I put forward (qaddamtu) in it" when I spoke about it.

The majority read ﴿لا تُقَدِّمُوا﴾ (do not put forward). It is possible that it is transitive, and its object was omitted so that it would encompass everything that comes to mind of what is put forward, not aiming at a specific thing. The prohibition relates to the act itself without specifying a particular object, like their saying: "So-and-so gives and withholds." It is also possible that it is intransitive, in the sense of taqaddama (to advance), as you say: "wajh" in the sense of "tawajjaha" (to head toward), and the omitted element would be something reached by a preposition, meaning: do not advance in any matter whatsoever, or in what they love. This interpretation is supported by the reading of Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Haywah, al-Dahhak, Ya'qub and Ibn Miqsam: ﴿لا تَقَدَّمُوا﴾ with fatah on the ta', qaf and dal, indicating intransitivity, and the ta' was dropped for lightness, since the original is "la tatqaddamu."

Some of the Meccan readers read: "taqaddamu" with shaddah on the ta', the ta' of the present tense assimilated into the following ta', like the reading of al-Bazzi. It was also read: ﴿لا تَقْدِمُوا﴾, the present tense of qadima with kasr on the dal, from al-qudum (arrival), meaning: do not come forward to a matter of the affairs of religion before its arrival, and do not hasten regarding it.

Al-makan al-musamit wajh ar-rajul (the place facing a man's face) means near him. It has been said: in the phrase "bayna yadayi" (before me) with respect to the one sitting before whom, there is a broadening, as it encompasses the two directions of right and left. In His words ﴿بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ﴾ (before Allah), it is a metaphor of a metaphor of the figurative representation. The purpose of depicting the vileness and ugliness in it: they were forbidden from advancing into a matter without being guided by the models of the Book and the Sunnah. The meaning is: do not decide any matter except after they (Allah and His Messenger) have ruled on it and permitted it, so that you act by the revelation sent down, or follow the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This, and on this rests the interpretation of Ibn 'Abbas. Mujahid said: "Do not invent anything against Allah until Allah relates it through the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ)." In this prohibition there is a preparation for what comes after it: their being forbidden to raise their voices. When He forbade, He commanded taqwa, because part of taqwa is avoiding what is forbidden.

﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ﴾ (Indeed Allah is All-Hearing) of your words, ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ (All-Knowing) of your intentions and your deeds.

Then He called them a second time, to stir what He casts to them, to emphasize the improbability of the rulings that keep arising, and to make them attentive to listening. It was revealed because of the custom of the Bedouins of harshness and raising the voice.

﴿لا تَرْفَعُوا أصْواتَكُمْ﴾ means: when he speaks and you speak, (p-106) ﴿ولا تَجْهَرُوا لَهُ بِالقَوْلِ﴾ (nor speak loudly to him in speech) when you address him, because the rank of prophethood and messengership must be honored and glorified, and speech with the Messenger (ﷺ) should not be like speech with others. When it was revealed, Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "O Messenger of Allah, I will not speak to you except in a whisper, or like one who whispers, until I meet Allah." "It is narrated from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) that he would speak to the Prophet (ﷺ) like one who whispers, not making him hear until he asked him to repeat." Whenever Abu Bakr came before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)... [the text here reads: "وكانَ أبُو بَكْرٍ إذا قَدِمَ عَلى الرَّسُولِ ﷺ، قَوْمٌ أرْسَلَ إلَيْهِمْ مَن يُعَلِّمُهم كَيْفَ يُسْلِمُونَ"]

Whenever Abu Bakr came before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a people, he sent to them someone who would teach them how to embrace Islam, and he commanded them to tranquility and dignity in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Raising the voice and loudness were nothing but what was in their natures, not that it was intended by that to show contempt or arrogance, for that would have made their action disbelief, and the addressees were believers.

﴿كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكم لِبَعْضٍ﴾ (like the loudness of some of you to others): meaning in lack of concern and little respect. They were only forbidden from a specific kind of loudness. The scholars disliked raising the voice at the grave of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in the presence of a scholar, and in the mosques.

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: it was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who had a deafness in his ear and was loud of voice. His cutting himself off in his house for days because of this is well known, and he said: "O Messenger of Allah, when it was revealed, I feared that my deeds would be nullified." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Indeed you are among the people of Paradise." He also said to him once: "Are you not pleased to live praiseworthy and die a martyr?" He lived thus, then he was killed at al-Yamamah, on the day of Musaylimah, may Allah be pleased with him.

﴿أنْ تَحْبَطَ أعْمالُكُمْ﴾ (lest your deeds be nullified): if the verse is directed at one who raises his voice out of contempt, then that is disbelief, by which the deed is truly nullified. If it is addressed to the believer who does that out of heedlessness and following his habit, then what is nullified is only the righteousness of honoring the Prophet (ﷺ) and lowering the voice in his presence, had he done that. It is as if He said: lest the deeds that you were prepared to do, so that you would be rewarded for them, be nullified. "Lest be nullified" (an tahbata) is an object of purpose, and the governing element is "wa la tajharu" according to the Basran school of preference, and "wa la tarfa'u" according to the Kufan school of preference. Nevertheless, in terms of meaning, the nullification of the deed is a cause in both raising and loudness. 'Abdullah and Zayd ibn 'Ali read: ﴿فَتَحْبَطَ﴾ with the fa', which is a consequence of what precedes it.

﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أصْواتَهُمْ﴾ (Indeed those who lower their voices): it was said: it was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), because of what came from them of lowering the voice and of reaching the point of speaking to him like one who whispers.

**Note on the text:** The Arabic passage above contains an incomplete sentence in the original ("وكانَ أبُو بَكْرٍ إذا قَدِمَ عَلى الرَّسُولِ ﷺ، قَوْمٌ أرْسَلَ إلَيْهِمْ") which I have rendered as it stands; the translation has been completed in its most literal reading.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 49, verses 1–5 (part 2 of 2):

﴿Allah has tested their hearts for piety﴾: meaning, they were tried and trained for piety, so they are fit for it. Or the word "testing" is used in the sense of "knowing," because the verification of a thing comes through testing it, so the meaning is that He knew their hearts to be devoted to piety. Or it means that Allah struck their hearts with various kinds of trials for the sake of piety, so that their piety would be firm and manifest. It has also been said that it means He purified them for piety, from the expression "he tested (imtahana) the gold and refined it (fatana)," meaning when he melted it and so separated its pure essence from its impurities. In this verse, "inna" (indeed, a particle of emphasis) is used to confirm the content of the sentence, and its predicate is a sentence beginning with the demonstrative noun, which indicates exaltation and definiteness, followed by the mention of their reward for lowering their voices. All of this is evidence that Allah is pleased with what they did in showing reverence to the Prophet ﷺ by lowering their voices. In it there is also an implicit rebuke of the enormity of what those who raised their voices committed, and a contrast with what those people deserved.

«﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the chambers﴾: It was revealed concerning the delegation of Banu Tamim, including al-Aqra' ibn Habis, al-Zibriqan ibn Badr, Amr ibn al-Ahtam and others. They came as a delegation and entered the mosque at midday while the Messenger ﷺ was sleeping. They began calling out to him all together: "O Muhammad, come out to us!" He awoke and came out, and al-Aqra' ibn Habis said to him: "O Muhammad, my praise is an adornment and my blame is a disgrace." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Woe to you, that is Allah, the Exalted." The people gathered in the mosque and said: "We are Banu Tamim, with our orator and our poet. We will compete with you in poetry and boast against you." The Prophet ﷺ said: "I was not sent with poetry, nor was I commanded to boast. But bring forth [what you have]." Al-Zibriqan said to a young man among them: "Boast and mention the virtue of your people." He said: "Praise be to Allah, who made us the best of His creation and gave us wealth with which we do as we please. We are among the best people on earth, the most numerous in number, wealth (p. 107) and weapons. Whoever denies this against us, let him bring a statement better than our statement and an action better than our action." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who was their orator: "Stand up and answer him." He said: "Praise be to Allah, I praise Him, seek His help, believe in Him and put my trust in Him, and I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. He called the emigrants from his own clan, the best of people in faces and the greatest of them in forbearance, and they answered him. Praise be to Allah, who made us the helpers of His religion, the ministers of His Messenger and a might for His religion. We fight the people until they testify that there is no god but Allah. Whoever says it protects his life and property, and whoever refuses it we kill, and that is a humiliation upon us that is easy for us. I say this statement of mine and I seek forgiveness from Allah for the believing men and believing women." Al-Zibriqan said to a young man: "Stand up and recite verses mentioning the virtue of your people." He said:

﴾We are the noble; there is no tribe equal to us; among us are the chiefs, and among us is the quarter (of the spoils) divided.﴿
﴾And we feed all of them in time of drought, from the choicest meat, when there is no comfort for the terrified.﴿
﴾When we refuse, none refuses for us; indeed, thus we are raised high at the time of boasting.﴿

The Prophet ﷺ gave an order, and he summoned Hassan ibn Thabit and said to him: "Repeat your statement to me so that I may hear it." Hassan answered:

﴾Indeed, the chiefs of Fihr and their brothers have established a practice that is followed by people.﴿
﴾Every man whose inner nature is the fear of Allah is advised to adopt it, for all good comes to light from it.﴿

Then Hassan said in some verses:

﴾We helped the Messenger of Allah and the religion by force, despite the wrath of the arrogant ones from Ma'add and the settled.﴿
﴾With blows like the kinds of she-camels' milk-bags, their marrow, and with spears like the mouths of the milch-camels being milked.﴾
﴾And ask Uhud on the day their hosts fled from blows we dealt them like the fierce lions.﴿
﴾Do we not plunge into death in the thick of battle, when the drinking of death is sweet among the warriors?﴿
﴾So we strike skulls with the two arms, belonging to a noble lineage from the trunk of Ghassan, resplendent.﴿
﴾Had it not been for shame before Allah, we would have said, out of generosity to the people, with both truths: "Is there any challenger?"﴿
﴾So our living are of the best who ever trod the pebbles, and our dead are of the best people of the graveyards.﴿

He said: Al-Aqra' ibn Habis then stood and said: "By Allah, I have indeed come for a matter, and I have composed a poem, so listen to it," and he said:

﴾We came to you so that the people would know our virtue, when they oppose us in mentioning noble deeds.﴿
﴾And indeed we are the heads of the people in every raid that takes place in Najd or the lands of the Tihama.﴿
﴾And indeed we have the mirba' (the one-quarter of the spoils) in every gathering, and no one in the land of Hijaz is like Darim.﴿

The Prophet ﷺ said to Hassan: "Stand up and answer him." He stood and said:

﴾Banu Darim, do not boast, for your boasting will become a calamity at the mention of noble deeds.﴿
﴾You are fools to boast against us, while you are for us slaves, between a wet-nurse and a servant.﴿

The Prophet ﷺ said: "You were indeed rich, O brother of Darim, that there should be mentioned from you what I thought the people had already disregarded." His statement ﷺ was harder upon them than everything Hassan had said. Then Hassan returned to his poetry and said:

﴾If you have come to protect your lives and your wealth from being divided among the shares,﴿
﴾then do not make a rival to Allah, and submit, and do not boast before the Prophet with Darim.﴿
﴾Otherwise, by the Lord of the House, the spears have leaned over your heads with sharp, keen swords.﴿

Al-Aqra' ibn Habis said: "By Allah, I do not know what this matter is. Our orator spoke, and their orator was better in speech, and our poet spoke, and their poet was more eloquent and better in speech." Then he drew near the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah." The Prophet ﷺ said: "What was before this will not harm you." Then he gave them and clothed them.»

The connection of this verse with what precedes it is clear: calling out from behind the chambers involves raising the voice and bad manners, while Allah has commanded the showing of reverence and honor to His Messenger. "Al-warā'" (behind) is the direction that a person is hidden from you by, whether from behind or in front, and "min" (from) indicates the starting point, and the calling out arose from that place. Al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask, what is the difference between the two statements, between that in which the one calling and the one called are both included by 'behind' and that in which they are not? I say: the difference between them is that in one of them the one called and the caller may both be encompassed by 'behind,' while in the second that is not permitted, because 'behind' becomes the starting point of the extent when preceded by 'min,' and it is not possible for the same direction to be both the starting point and the endpoint for a single action. One who says, 'So-and-so called me from behind the house,' does not mean the front of the house nor its back, but any side of its sides, without specifying or restricting it." End of quotation. Our scholars have established, in the meanings of "min," that it may indicate the starting point and the endpoint in a single action, and that the same thing may be the locus of both. They interpreted this in accordance with Sibawayh, saying: from this is their saying, "I took the dirham from Zayd," where Zayd is the locus for both the beginning of the taking from him and its end together. They said: "min" indicates only the starting point in most cases, and in some cases it indicates both the starting point and the endpoint together. The calling that was condemned was not condemned because it occurred at the back of the chambers or at their fronts, but rather they were condemned because they called to him from outside in the manner of the uncouth, which contains no reverence, just as some of them call to one another.

And "al-ḥujurāt" (the chambers): these were the dwellings of the Messenger ﷺ, and there were nine of them. "Al-ḥujrah" is an elevated area of land enclosed by a wall that surrounds it, and the enclosure for camels is called "ḥujrah," and it is of the form "fu'lah" in the sense of "maf'ūlah" (passive participle), like "ghurfah" and "qabḍah." The majority recited "al-ḥujurāt" with a damma on the jim, following the damma before it. Abu Ja'far and Shayba recited it with a fatḥa, and Ibn Abi Abla recited it with a sukūn, and these are three dialects, in each case following the condition mentioned in the science of grammar. The apparent meaning is that those who made the calling were a group. Al-Asamm mentioned that the ones who called out to him were al-Aqra' ibn Habis and Uyayna ibn Hisn. If that is correct, then the attribution to the group is because they were content with it. And when they were a group, it is possible that they dispersed, so some called out from behind this chamber and some from behind that one, or they called out together from behind each chamber, or the chamber was one, and it was the one in which the Messenger ﷺ was, and it was made plural out of honor for him. The negation of reason from most of them is evidence that among them there is reason. Al-Zamakhshari said: "It is possible that the ruling about the scarcity of intelligent people among them is intended purposefully to negate that there is among them anyone who has understanding, for scarcity is often used in their speech in the sense of negation." End of quotation. In the verse there is no explicit statement of the scarcity of reason, so negation could be understood, but it is only implied by His saying: ﴿most of them do not understand﴾. Pure negation is derived only from the explicit wording of scarcity, not from implication, so His saying: ﴿but most of mankind do not give thanks﴾ [al-Baqarah: 243] is not to be understood as pure negation of thankfulness, because the negation was not derived from the explicit scarcity. This verse was recorded against those who called to him with foolishness and ignorance.

He began the beginning of the surah by putting forward the matters that belong to Allah and His Messenger above all matters, and then above what He forbade of putting oneself forward, by forbidding raising the voice and loudness. So the first was a foundation for the second. Then it follows with what is praise of those who refrained from that, who lowered their voices, indicating the greatness of their standing with Allah. Then, following it, came what is more grievous, which is shouting to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in privacy with some of his household from behind the wall, as one shouts to the lowliest of people, so as to rebuke them for the awfulness of what they dared to do, because (p. 109) whoever Allah has raised in rank above being addressed in a loud voice, the conduct of these toward him was an extremely abominable wrong. From this and similar examples the excellent manners are derived. As is related from Abu Ubayd, whose standing in knowledge, asceticism and reliability of narration is well known, that he said: "I never knocked on the door of a scholar until he came out at the time of his coming out."

﴿And if they had been patient until you came out to them﴾: Al-Zamakhshari said: "'That they were patient' is in the position of the nominative by way of being the agent, because the meaning is: 'If their patience had been established.'" End of quotation. This is not the doctrine of Sibawayh, who held that "anna" and what follows it after "law" is in the position of the subject, not the position of the agent. The doctrine of al-Mubarrad is that it is in the position of an agent governed by a deleted verb, as al-Zamakhshari claimed. The subject of "kāna" is a pronoun referring to the verbal noun understood from "ṣabarū," meaning "it would have been"; that is, their patience would have been better for them. Al-Zamakhshari said: "In 'kāna,' it is either a pronoun for the agent of the verb implied after 'law.'" End of quotation, because he estimated that "anna" and what follows it is an agent of a hidden verb, so he returned the pronoun to that agent, which is the patience formed from "anna" and its complement, "better for them" in reward with Allah, and in the expansion of the soul of the Messenger ﷺ and in his fulfilling their needs. It has been said that they came as captives, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ freed half and ransomed half, and had they been patient he would have freed all of them without ransom. It has also been said: "Their patience would have been better for their manners."

﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: His forgiveness and mercy will not be too narrow for these people if they repent and turn back in penitence.

(سُورَةُ الحُجُراتِ ثَمانِيَ عَشْرَةَ آيَةً مَدَنِيَّةٌ)
(بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ)

(p-104) ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَرْفَعُوا أصْواتَكم فَوْقَ صَوْتِ النَّبِيِّ ولا تَجْهَرُوا لَهُ بِالقَوْلِ كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكم لِبَعْضٍ أنْ تَحْبَطَ أعْمالُكم وأنْتُمْ لا تَشْعُرُونَ﴾ ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أصْواتَهم عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ امْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهم لِلتَّقْوى لَهم مَغْفِرَةٌ وأجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يُنادُونَكَ مِن وراءِ الحُجُراتِ أكْثَرُهم لا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ ﴿ولَوْ أنَّهم صَبَرُوا حَتّى تَخْرُجَ إلَيْهِمْ لَكانَ خَيْرًا لَهم واللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إنْ جاءَكم فاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوا أنْ تُصِيبُوا قَوْمًا بِجَهالَةٍ فَتُصْبِحُوا عَلى ما فَعَلْتُمْ نادِمِينَ﴾ [الحجرات: 6] ﴿واعْلَمُوا أنَّ فِيكم رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لَوْ يُطِيعُكم في كَثِيرٍ مِنَ الأمْرِ لَعَنِتُّمْ ولَكِنَّ اللَّهَ حَبَّبَ إلَيْكُمُ الإيمانَ وزَيَّنَهُ في قُلُوبِكم وكَرَّهَ إلَيْكُمُ الكُفْرَ والفُسُوقَ والعِصْيانَ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الرّاشِدُونَ﴾ [الحجرات: 7] ﴿فَضْلًا مِنَ اللَّهِ ونِعْمَةً واللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ [الحجرات: 8] ﴿وإنْ طائِفَتانِ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا فَأصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُما فَإنْ بَغَتْ إحْداهُما عَلى الأُخْرى فَقاتِلُوا الَّتِي تَبْغِي حَتّى تَفِيءَ إلى أمْرِ اللَّهِ فَإنْ فاءَتْ فَأصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُما بِالعَدْلِ وأقْسِطُوا إنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ المُقْسِطِينَ﴾ [الحجرات: 9] ﴿إنَّما المُؤْمِنُونَ إخْوَةٌ فَأصْلِحُوا بَيْنَ أخَوَيْكم واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكم تُرْحَمُونَ﴾ [الحجرات: 10] ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِن قَوْمٍ عَسى أنْ يَكُونُوا خَيْرًا مِنهم ولا نِساءٌ مِن نِساءٍ عَسى أنْ يَكُنَّ خَيْرًا مِنهُنَّ ولا تَلْمِزُوا أنْفُسَكم ولا تَنابَزُوا بِالألْقابِ بِئْسَ الِاسْمُ الفُسُوقُ بَعْدَ الإيمانِ ومَن لَمْ يَتُبْ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الظّالِمُونَ﴾ [الحجرات: 11] ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيرًا مِنَ الظَّنِّ إنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إثْمٌ ولا تَجَسَّسُوا ولا يَغْتَبْ بَعْضُكم بَعْضًا أيُحِبُّ أحَدُكم أنْ يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أخِيهِ مَيْتًا فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إنَّ اللَّهَ تَوّابٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [الحجرات: 12] ﴿يا أيُّها النّاسُ إنّا خَلَقْناكم مِن ذَكَرٍ وأُنْثى وجَعَلْناكم شُعُوبًا وقَبائِلَ لِتَعارَفُوا إنَّ أكْرَمَكم عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أتْقاكم إنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ﴾ [الحجرات: 13] ﴿قالَتِ الأعْرابُ آمَنّا قُلْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا ولَكِنْ قُولُوا أسْلَمْنا ولَمّا يَدْخُلِ الإيمانُ في قُلُوبِكم وإنْ تُطِيعُوا اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ لا يَلِتْكم مِن أعْمالِكم شَيْئًا إنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [الحجرات: 14] ﴿إنَّما المُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَرْتابُوا وجاهَدُوا بِأمْوالِهِمْ وأنْفُسِهِمْ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الصّادِقُونَ﴾ [الحجرات: 15] ﴿قُلْ أتُعَلِّمُونَ اللَّهَ بِدِينِكم واللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ واللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ [الحجرات: 16] ﴿يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ أنْ أسْلَمُوا قُلْ لا تَمُنُّوا عَلَيَّ إسْلامَكم بَلِ اللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيْكم أنْ هَداكم لِلْإيمانِ إنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ﴾ [الحجرات: 17] ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ واللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [الحجرات: 18]

At-tanabuz bil-alqab (mutual nicknaming): calling one another by it; it is of the form tafa'ala from nabazahu. The Banu Fulan yatanabazuna and yatanazabuna. It is said: an-nabz and an-nazb are the bad nickname.

Al-laqab (nickname) is what a person is called by, other than his given name or his kunyah (teknonym). It is of two kinds: ugly, which is what a person dislikes because it belittles him and is a reproach; and good, which is the opposite, such as as-Siddiq for Abu Bakr, al-Faruq for Umar, and Asad Allah (Lion of God) for Hamzah, may Allah be pleased with them.

Tajassasa al-amr: he sought it out and searched for its hidden aspects. It is from the root jass, and from it comes al-jasus (spy), who searches for the faults in order to know them. The senses of a person are called al-hawass, with ha' and jim.

Ash-sha'b (nation): the first of the six levels into which the Arabs were divided, namely: ash-sha'b, al-qabilah (tribe), al-'imarah (clan), al-batn (sub-clan), al-fakhdh (branch), and al-fasilah (subdivision). Thus ash-sha'b includes the qaba'il, the qabilah includes the 'amā'ir, the 'imarah includes the butun, the batn includes the afkhadh, and the fakhdh includes the fasa'il. Khuzaymah is a sha'b, Kinanah is a qabilah, Quraysh is an 'imarah, Qusayy is a batn, Hashim is a fakhdh, and al-Abbas is a fasilah. The term shu'ub was so named because the tribes branched out (tasha''abat) from them. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "ash-shu'ub" means the butun (sub-clans). This is other than what the lexicographers have agreed upon, and a disagreement on this will come up at His words: ﴿وجَعَلْناكم شُعُوبًا﴾ [49:13].

Al-qabilah is below ash-sha'b; it is likened to the qaba'il of the head (the sutures of the skull), because they are pieces that face one another.

Alta yaaltu: with damm and kasr of the lam, alta (also), and lata yalitu and alata yaliitu (quadriliteral): three dialects transmitted by Abu 'Ubaydah, and the meaning is "he fell short." Ru'bah said:

"And a night full of dew I travelled, and the lion did not hold me back from its journey."

That is: it did not prevent me nor restrain me. Al-Hutay'ah said:

"Convey to the nobles of Banu Sa'd, with the utmost effort of the message, without shortfall or lie."

(p-105) ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ ﴿ياأيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَرْفَعُوا أصْواتَكم فَوْقَ صَوْتِ النَّبِيِّ ولا تَجْهَرُوا لَهُ بِالقَوْلِ كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكم لِبَعْضٍ أنْ تَحْبَطَ أعْمالُكم وأنْتُمْ لا تَشْعُرُونَ﴾ ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أصْواتَهم عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ امْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهم لِلتَّقْوى لَهم مَغْفِرَةٌ وأجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يُنادُونَكَ مِن وراءِ الحُجُراتِ أكْثَرُهم لا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ ﴿ولَوْ أنَّهم صَبَرُوا حَتّى تَخْرُجَ إلَيْهِمْ لَكانَ خَيْرًا لَهم واللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ ﴿ياأيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إنْ جاءَكم فاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوا أنْ تُصِيبُوا قَوْمًا بِجَهالَةٍ فَتُصْبِحُوا عَلى ما فَعَلْتُمْ نادِمِينَ﴾ [الحجرات: 6] ﴿واعْلَمُوا أنَّ فِيكم رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لَوْ يُطِيعُكم في كَثِيرٍ مِنَ الأمْرِ لَعَنِتُّمْ ولَكِنَّ اللَّهَ حَبَّبَ إلَيْكُمُ الإيمانَ وزَيَّنَهُ في قُلُوبِكم وكَرَّهَ إلَيْكُمُ الكُفْرَ والفُسُوقَ والعِصْيانَ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الرّاشِدُونَ﴾ [الحجرات: 7] ﴿فَضْلًا مِنَ اللَّهِ ونِعْمَةً واللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ [الحجرات: 8].

This surah is Medinan. Its connection with what precedes it is evident, because He mentioned the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions, then said: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [48:29]. So perhaps some of the believers who do righteous deeds did something that ought to be forbidden, and so the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, do not put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾.

It was the custom of the Arabs, and it remains so to this day, to share opinions, for each to speak as he wishes and do what he loves. Some of those who had not trained themselves in the etiquette of the Sharia did some of this. Qatadah said: "Some people would say: it should be such-and-such if such-and-such were revealed." Al-Hasan said: "A people slaughtered sacrifices before the Prophet (ﷺ), and a people did something on their own opinion during one of his campaigns, so this verse was revealed forbidding all of that." Ibn 'Abbas said: "They were forbidden to speak before his speech." The Arabs say: "I went ahead (taqaddamtu) in such-and-such," and "I put forward (qaddamtu) in it" when I spoke about it.

The majority read ﴿لا تُقَدِّمُوا﴾ (do not put forward). It is possible that it is transitive, and its object was omitted so that it would encompass everything that comes to mind of what is put forward, not aiming at a specific thing. The prohibition relates to the act itself without specifying a particular object, like their saying: "So-and-so gives and withholds." It is also possible that it is intransitive, in the sense of taqaddama (to advance), as you say: "wajh" in the sense of "tawajjaha" (to head toward), and the omitted element would be something reached by a preposition, meaning: do not advance in any matter whatsoever, or in what they love. This interpretation is supported by the reading of Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Haywah, al-Dahhak, Ya'qub and Ibn Miqsam: ﴿لا تَقَدَّمُوا﴾ with fatah on the ta', qaf and dal, indicating intransitivity, and the ta' was dropped for lightness, since the original is "la tatqaddamu."

Some of the Meccan readers read: "taqaddamu" with shaddah on the ta', the ta' of the present tense assimilated into the following ta', like the reading of al-Bazzi. It was also read: ﴿لا تَقْدِمُوا﴾, the present tense of qadima with kasr on the dal, from al-qudum (arrival), meaning: do not come forward to a matter of the affairs of religion before its arrival, and do not hasten regarding it.

Al-makan al-musamit wajh ar-rajul (the place facing a man's face) means near him. It has been said: in the phrase "bayna yadayi" (before me) with respect to the one sitting before whom, there is a broadening, as it encompasses the two directions of right and left. In His words ﴿بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ﴾ (before Allah), it is a metaphor of a metaphor of the figurative representation. The purpose of depicting the vileness and ugliness in it: they were forbidden from advancing into a matter without being guided by the models of the Book and the Sunnah. The meaning is: do not decide any matter except after they (Allah and His Messenger) have ruled on it and permitted it, so that you act by the revelation sent down, or follow the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This, and on this rests the interpretation of Ibn 'Abbas. Mujahid said: "Do not invent anything against Allah until Allah relates it through the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ)." In this prohibition there is a preparation for what comes after it: their being forbidden to raise their voices. When He forbade, He commanded taqwa, because part of taqwa is avoiding what is forbidden.

﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ﴾ (Indeed Allah is All-Hearing) of your words, ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ (All-Knowing) of your intentions and your deeds.

Then He called them a second time, to stir what He casts to them, to emphasize the improbability of the rulings that keep arising, and to make them attentive to listening. It was revealed because of the custom of the Bedouins of harshness and raising the voice.

﴿لا تَرْفَعُوا أصْواتَكُمْ﴾ means: when he speaks and you speak, (p-106) ﴿ولا تَجْهَرُوا لَهُ بِالقَوْلِ﴾ (nor speak loudly to him in speech) when you address him, because the rank of prophethood and messengership must be honored and glorified, and speech with the Messenger (ﷺ) should not be like speech with others. When it was revealed, Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "O Messenger of Allah, I will not speak to you except in a whisper, or like one who whispers, until I meet Allah." "It is narrated from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) that he would speak to the Prophet (ﷺ) like one who whispers, not making him hear until he asked him to repeat." Whenever Abu Bakr came before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)... [the text here reads: "وكانَ أبُو بَكْرٍ إذا قَدِمَ عَلى الرَّسُولِ ﷺ، قَوْمٌ أرْسَلَ إلَيْهِمْ مَن يُعَلِّمُهم كَيْفَ يُسْلِمُونَ"]

Whenever Abu Bakr came before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a people, he sent to them someone who would teach them how to embrace Islam, and he commanded them to tranquility and dignity in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Raising the voice and loudness were nothing but what was in their natures, not that it was intended by that to show contempt or arrogance, for that would have made their action disbelief, and the addressees were believers.

﴿كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكم لِبَعْضٍ﴾ (like the loudness of some of you to others): meaning in lack of concern and little respect. They were only forbidden from a specific kind of loudness. The scholars disliked raising the voice at the grave of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in the presence of a scholar, and in the mosques.

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: it was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who had a deafness in his ear and was loud of voice. His cutting himself off in his house for days because of this is well known, and he said: "O Messenger of Allah, when it was revealed, I feared that my deeds would be nullified." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Indeed you are among the people of Paradise." He also said to him once: "Are you not pleased to live praiseworthy and die a martyr?" He lived thus, then he was killed at al-Yamamah, on the day of Musaylimah, may Allah be pleased with him.

﴿أنْ تَحْبَطَ أعْمالُكُمْ﴾ (lest your deeds be nullified): if the verse is directed at one who raises his voice out of contempt, then that is disbelief, by which the deed is truly nullified. If it is addressed to the believer who does that out of heedlessness and following his habit, then what is nullified is only the righteousness of honoring the Prophet (ﷺ) and lowering the voice in his presence, had he done that. It is as if He said: lest the deeds that you were prepared to do, so that you would be rewarded for them, be nullified. "Lest be nullified" (an tahbata) is an object of purpose, and the governing element is "wa la tajharu" according to the Basran school of preference, and "wa la tarfa'u" according to the Kufan school of preference. Nevertheless, in terms of meaning, the nullification of the deed is a cause in both raising and loudness. 'Abdullah and Zayd ibn 'Ali read: ﴿فَتَحْبَطَ﴾ with the fa', which is a consequence of what precedes it.

﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أصْواتَهُمْ﴾ (Indeed those who lower their voices): it was said: it was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), because of what came from them of lowering the voice and of reaching the point of speaking to him like one who whispers.

---

**Note on the text:** The Arabic passage above contains an incomplete sentence in the original ("وكانَ أبُو بَكْرٍ إذا قَدِمَ عَلى الرَّسُولِ ﷺ، قَوْمٌ أرْسَلَ إلَيْهِمْ") which I have rendered as it stands; the translation has been completed in its most literal reading.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 49, verses 1–5 (part 2 of 2):

﴿Allah has tested their hearts for piety﴾: meaning, they were tried and trained for piety, so they are fit for it. Or the word "testing" is used in the sense of "knowing," because the verification of a thing comes through testing it, so the meaning is that He knew their hearts to be devoted to piety. Or it means that Allah struck their hearts with various kinds of trials for the sake of piety, so that their piety would be firm and manifest. It has also been said that it means He purified them for piety, from the expression "he tested (imtahana) the gold and refined it (fatana)," meaning when he melted it and so separated its pure essence from its impurities. In this verse, "inna" (indeed, a particle of emphasis) is used to confirm the content of the sentence, and its predicate is a sentence beginning with the demonstrative noun, which indicates exaltation and definiteness, followed by the mention of their reward for lowering their voices. All of this is evidence that Allah is pleased with what they did in showing reverence to the Prophet ﷺ by lowering their voices. In it there is also an implicit rebuke of the enormity of what those who raised their voices committed, and a contrast with what those people deserved.

«﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the chambers﴾: It was revealed concerning the delegation of Banu Tamim, including al-Aqra' ibn Habis, al-Zibriqan ibn Badr, Amr ibn al-Ahtam and others. They came as a delegation and entered the mosque at midday while the Messenger ﷺ was sleeping. They began calling out to him all together: "O Muhammad, come out to us!" He awoke and came out, and al-Aqra' ibn Habis said to him: "O Muhammad, my praise is an adornment and my blame is a disgrace." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Woe to you, that is Allah, the Exalted." The people gathered in the mosque and said: "We are Banu Tamim, with our orator and our poet. We will compete with you in poetry and boast against you." The Prophet ﷺ said: "I was not sent with poetry, nor was I commanded to boast. But bring forth [what you have]." Al-Zibriqan said to a young man among them: "Boast and mention the virtue of your people." He said: "Praise be to Allah, who made us the best of His creation and gave us wealth with which we do as we please. We are among the best people on earth, the most numerous in number, wealth (p. 107) and weapons. Whoever denies this against us, let him bring a statement better than our statement and an action better than our action." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who was their orator: "Stand up and answer him." He said: "Praise be to Allah, I praise Him, seek His help, believe in Him and put my trust in Him, and I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. He called the emigrants from his own clan, the best of people in faces and the greatest of them in forbearance, and they answered him. Praise be to Allah, who made us the helpers of His religion, the ministers of His Messenger and a might for His religion. We fight the people until they testify that there is no god but Allah. Whoever says it protects his life and property, and whoever refuses it we kill, and that is a humiliation upon us that is easy for us. I say this statement of mine and I seek forgiveness from Allah for the believing men and believing women." Al-Zibriqan said to a young man: "Stand up and recite verses mentioning the virtue of your people." He said:

﴾We are the noble; there is no tribe equal to us; among us are the chiefs, and among us is the quarter (of the spoils) divided.﴿
﴾And we feed all of them in time of drought, from the choicest meat, when there is no comfort for the terrified.﴿
﴾When we refuse, none refuses for us; indeed, thus we are raised high at the time of boasting.﴿

The Prophet ﷺ gave an order, and he summoned Hassan ibn Thabit and said to him: "Repeat your statement to me so that I may hear it." Hassan answered:

﴾Indeed, the chiefs of Fihr and their brothers have established a practice that is followed by people.﴿
﴾Every man whose inner nature is the fear of Allah is advised to adopt it, for all good comes to light from it.﴿

Then Hassan said in some verses:

﴾We helped the Messenger of Allah and the religion by force, despite the wrath of the arrogant ones from Ma'add and the settled.﴿
﴾With blows like the kinds of she-camels' milk-bags, their marrow, and with spears like the mouths of the milch-camels being milked.﴾
﴾And ask Uhud on the day their hosts fled from blows we dealt them like the fierce lions.﴿
﴾Do we not plunge into death in the thick of battle, when the drinking of death is sweet among the warriors?﴿
﴾So we strike skulls with the two arms, belonging to a noble lineage from the trunk of Ghassan, resplendent.﴿
﴾Had it not been for shame before Allah, we would have said, out of generosity to the people, with both truths: "Is there any challenger?"﴿
﴾So our living are of the best who ever trod the pebbles, and our dead are of the best people of the graveyards.﴿

He said: Al-Aqra' ibn Habis then stood and said: "By Allah, I have indeed come for a matter, and I have composed a poem, so listen to it," and he said:

﴾We came to you so that the people would know our virtue, when they oppose us in mentioning noble deeds.﴿
﴾And indeed we are the heads of the people in every raid that takes place in Najd or the lands of the Tihama.﴿
﴾And indeed we have the mirba' (the one-quarter of the spoils) in every gathering, and no one in the land of Hijaz is like Darim.﴿

The Prophet ﷺ said to Hassan: "Stand up and answer him." He stood and said:

﴾Banu Darim, do not boast, for your boasting will become a calamity at the mention of noble deeds.﴿
﴾You are fools to boast against us, while you are for us slaves, between a wet-nurse and a servant.﴿

The Prophet ﷺ said: "You were indeed rich, O brother of Darim, that there should be mentioned from you what I thought the people had already disregarded." His statement ﷺ was harder upon them than everything Hassan had said. Then Hassan returned to his poetry and said:

﴾If you have come to protect your lives and your wealth from being divided among the shares,﴿
﴾then do not make a rival to Allah, and submit, and do not boast before the Prophet with Darim.﴿
﴾Otherwise, by the Lord of the House, the spears have leaned over your heads with sharp, keen swords.﴿

Al-Aqra' ibn Habis said: "By Allah, I do not know what this matter is. Our orator spoke, and their orator was better in speech, and our poet spoke, and their poet was more eloquent and better in speech." Then he drew near the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah." The Prophet ﷺ said: "What was before this will not harm you." Then he gave them and clothed them.»

The connection of this verse with what precedes it is clear: calling out from behind the chambers involves raising the voice and bad manners, while Allah has commanded the showing of reverence and honor to His Messenger. "Al-warā'" (behind) is the direction that a person is hidden from you by, whether from behind or in front, and "min" (from) indicates the starting point, and the calling out arose from that place. Al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask, what is the difference between the two statements, between that in which the one calling and the one called are both included by 'behind' and that in which they are not? I say: the difference between them is that in one of them the one called and the caller may both be encompassed by 'behind,' while in the second that is not permitted, because 'behind' becomes the starting point of the extent when preceded by 'min,' and it is not possible for the same direction to be both the starting point and the endpoint for a single action. One who says, 'So-and-so called me from behind the house,' does not mean the front of the house nor its back, but any side of its sides, without specifying or restricting it." End of quotation. Our scholars have established, in the meanings of "min," that it may indicate the starting point and the endpoint in a single action, and that the same thing may be the locus of both. They interpreted this in accordance with Sibawayh, saying: from this is their saying, "I took the dirham from Zayd," where Zayd is the locus for both the beginning of the taking from him and its end together. They said: "min" indicates only the starting point in most cases, and in some cases it indicates both the starting point and the endpoint together. The calling that was condemned was not condemned because it occurred at the back of the chambers or at their fronts, but rather they were condemned because they called to him from outside in the manner of the uncouth, which contains no reverence, just as some of them call to one another.

And "al-ḥujurāt" (the chambers): these were the dwellings of the Messenger ﷺ, and there were nine of them. "Al-ḥujrah" is an elevated area of land enclosed by a wall that surrounds it, and the enclosure for camels is called "ḥujrah," and it is of the form "fu'lah" in the sense of "maf'ūlah" (passive participle), like "ghurfah" and "qabḍah." The majority recited "al-ḥujurāt" with a damma on the jim, following the damma before it. Abu Ja'far and Shayba recited it with a fatḥa, and Ibn Abi Abla recited it with a sukūn, and these are three dialects, in each case following the condition mentioned in the science of grammar. The apparent meaning is that those who made the calling were a group. Al-Asamm mentioned that the ones who called out to him were al-Aqra' ibn Habis and Uyayna ibn Hisn. If that is correct, then the attribution to the group is because they were content with it. And when they were a group, it is possible that they dispersed, so some called out from behind this chamber and some from behind that one, or they called out together from behind each chamber, or the chamber was one, and it was the one in which the Messenger ﷺ was, and it was made plural out of honor for him. The negation of reason from most of them is evidence that among them there is reason. Al-Zamakhshari said: "It is possible that the ruling about the scarcity of intelligent people among them is intended purposefully to negate that there is among them anyone who has understanding, for scarcity is often used in their speech in the sense of negation." End of quotation. In the verse there is no explicit statement of the scarcity of reason, so negation could be understood, but it is only implied by His saying: ﴿most of them do not understand﴾. Pure negation is derived only from the explicit wording of scarcity, not from implication, so His saying: ﴿but most of mankind do not give thanks﴾ [al-Baqarah: 243] is not to be understood as pure negation of thankfulness, because the negation was not derived from the explicit scarcity. This verse was recorded against those who called to him with foolishness and ignorance.

He began the beginning of the surah by putting forward the matters that belong to Allah and His Messenger above all matters, and then above what He forbade of putting oneself forward, by forbidding raising the voice and loudness. So the first was a foundation for the second. Then it follows with what is praise of those who refrained from that, who lowered their voices, indicating the greatness of their standing with Allah. Then, following it, came what is more grievous, which is shouting to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in privacy with some of his household from behind the wall, as one shouts to the lowliest of people, so as to rebuke them for the awfulness of what they dared to do, because (p. 109) whoever Allah has raised in rank above being addressed in a loud voice, the conduct of these toward him was an extremely abominable wrong. From this and similar examples the excellent manners are derived. As is related from Abu Ubayd, whose standing in knowledge, asceticism and reliability of narration is well known, that he said: "I never knocked on the door of a scholar until he came out at the time of his coming out."

﴿And if they had been patient until you came out to them﴾: Al-Zamakhshari said: "'That they were patient' is in the position of the nominative by way of being the agent, because the meaning is: 'If their patience had been established.'" End of quotation. This is not the doctrine of Sibawayh, who held that "anna" and what follows it after "law" is in the position of the subject, not the position of the agent. The doctrine of al-Mubarrad is that it is in the position of an agent governed by a deleted verb, as al-Zamakhshari claimed. The subject of "kāna" is a pronoun referring to the verbal noun understood from "ṣabarū," meaning "it would have been"; that is, their patience would have been better for them. Al-Zamakhshari said: "In 'kāna,' it is either a pronoun for the agent of the verb implied after 'law.'" End of quotation, because he estimated that "anna" and what follows it is an agent of a hidden verb, so he returned the pronoun to that agent, which is the patience formed from "anna" and its complement, "better for them" in reward with Allah, and in the expansion of the soul of the Messenger ﷺ and in his fulfilling their needs. It has been said that they came as captives, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ freed half and ransomed half, and had they been patient he would have freed all of them without ransom. It has also been said: "Their patience would have been better for their manners."

﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: His forgiveness and mercy will not be too narrow for these people if they repent and turn back in penitence.

(سُورَةُ الحُجُراتِ ثَمانِيَ عَشْرَةَ آيَةً مَدَنِيَّةٌ)
(بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ)

(p-104) ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَرْفَعُوا أصْواتَكم فَوْقَ صَوْتِ النَّبِيِّ ولا تَجْهَرُوا لَهُ بِالقَوْلِ كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكم لِبَعْضٍ أنْ تَحْبَطَ أعْمالُكم وأنْتُمْ لا تَشْعُرُونَ﴾ ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أصْواتَهم عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ امْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهم لِلتَّقْوى لَهم مَغْفِرَةٌ وأجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يُنادُونَكَ مِن وراءِ الحُجُراتِ أكْثَرُهم لا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ ﴿ولَوْ أنَّهم صَبَرُوا حَتّى تَخْرُجَ إلَيْهِمْ لَكانَ خَيْرًا لَهم واللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إنْ جاءَكم فاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوا أنْ تُصِيبُوا قَوْمًا بِجَهالَةٍ فَتُصْبِحُوا عَلى ما فَعَلْتُمْ نادِمِينَ﴾ [الحجرات: 6] ﴿واعْلَمُوا أنَّ فِيكم رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لَوْ يُطِيعُكم في كَثِيرٍ مِنَ الأمْرِ لَعَنِتُّمْ ولَكِنَّ اللَّهَ حَبَّبَ إلَيْكُمُ الإيمانَ وزَيَّنَهُ في قُلُوبِكم وكَرَّهَ إلَيْكُمُ الكُفْرَ والفُسُوقَ والعِصْيانَ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الرّاشِدُونَ﴾ [الحجرات: 7] ﴿فَضْلًا مِنَ اللَّهِ ونِعْمَةً واللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ [الحجرات: 8] ﴿وإنْ طائِفَتانِ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا فَأصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُما فَإنْ بَغَتْ إحْداهُما عَلى الأُخْرى فَقاتِلُوا الَّتِي تَبْغِي حَتّى تَفِيءَ إلى أمْرِ اللَّهِ فَإنْ فاءَتْ فَأصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُما بِالعَدْلِ وأقْسِطُوا إنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ المُقْسِطِينَ﴾ [الحجرات: 9] ﴿إنَّما المُؤْمِنُونَ إخْوَةٌ فَأصْلِحُوا بَيْنَ أخَوَيْكم واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكم تُرْحَمُونَ﴾ [الحجرات: 10] ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِن قَوْمٍ عَسى أنْ يَكُونُوا خَيْرًا مِنهم ولا نِساءٌ مِن نِساءٍ عَسى أنْ يَكُنَّ خَيْرًا مِنهُنَّ ولا تَلْمِزُوا أنْفُسَكم ولا تَنابَزُوا بِالألْقابِ بِئْسَ الِاسْمُ الفُسُوقُ بَعْدَ الإيمانِ ومَن لَمْ يَتُبْ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الظّالِمُونَ﴾ [الحجرات: 11] ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيرًا مِنَ الظَّنِّ إنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إثْمٌ ولا تَجَسَّسُوا ولا يَغْتَبْ بَعْضُكم بَعْضًا أيُحِبُّ أحَدُكم أنْ يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أخِيهِ مَيْتًا فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إنَّ اللَّهَ تَوّابٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [الحجرات: 12] ﴿يا أيُّها النّاسُ إنّا خَلَقْناكم مِن ذَكَرٍ وأُنْثى وجَعَلْناكم شُعُوبًا وقَبائِلَ لِتَعارَفُوا إنَّ أكْرَمَكم عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أتْقاكم إنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ﴾ [الحجرات: 13] ﴿قالَتِ الأعْرابُ آمَنّا قُلْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا ولَكِنْ قُولُوا أسْلَمْنا ولَمّا يَدْخُلِ الإيمانُ في قُلُوبِكم وإنْ تُطِيعُوا اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ لا يَلِتْكم مِن أعْمالِكم شَيْئًا إنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [الحجرات: 14] ﴿إنَّما المُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَرْتابُوا وجاهَدُوا بِأمْوالِهِمْ وأنْفُسِهِمْ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الصّادِقُونَ﴾ [الحجرات: 15] ﴿قُلْ أتُعَلِّمُونَ اللَّهَ بِدِينِكم واللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ واللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ [الحجرات: 16] ﴿يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ أنْ أسْلَمُوا قُلْ لا تَمُنُّوا عَلَيَّ إسْلامَكم بَلِ اللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيْكم أنْ هَداكم لِلْإيمانِ إنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ﴾ [الحجرات: 17] ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ واللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [الحجرات: 18]

At-tanabuz bil-alqab (mutual nicknaming): calling one another by it; it is of the form tafa'ala from nabazahu. The Banu Fulan yatanabazuna and yatanazabuna. It is said: an-nabz and an-nazb are the bad nickname.

Al-laqab (nickname) is what a person is called by, other than his given name or his kunyah (teknonym). It is of two kinds: ugly, which is what a person dislikes because it belittles him and is a reproach; and good, which is the opposite, such as as-Siddiq for Abu Bakr, al-Faruq for Umar, and Asad Allah (Lion of God) for Hamzah, may Allah be pleased with them.

Tajassasa al-amr: he sought it out and searched for its hidden aspects. It is from the root jass, and from it comes al-jasus (spy), who searches for the faults in order to know them. The senses of a person are called al-hawass, with ha' and jim.

Ash-sha'b (nation): the first of the six levels into which the Arabs were divided, namely: ash-sha'b, al-qabilah (tribe), al-'imarah (clan), al-batn (sub-clan), al-fakhdh (branch), and al-fasilah (subdivision). Thus ash-sha'b includes the qaba'il, the qabilah includes the 'amā'ir, the 'imarah includes the butun, the batn includes the afkhadh, and the fakhdh includes the fasa'il. Khuzaymah is a sha'b, Kinanah is a qabilah, Quraysh is an 'imarah, Qusayy is a batn, Hashim is a fakhdh, and al-Abbas is a fasilah. The term shu'ub was so named because the tribes branched out (tasha''abat) from them. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "ash-shu'ub" means the butun (sub-clans). This is other than what the lexicographers have agreed upon, and a disagreement on this will come up at His words: ﴿وجَعَلْناكم شُعُوبًا﴾ [49:13].

Al-qabilah is below ash-sha'b; it is likened to the qaba'il of the head (the sutures of the skull), because they are pieces that face one another.

Alta yaaltu: with damm and kasr of the lam, alta (also), and lata yalitu and alata yaliitu (quadriliteral): three dialects transmitted by Abu 'Ubaydah, and the meaning is "he fell short." Ru'bah said:

"And a night full of dew I travelled, and the lion did not hold me back from its journey."

That is: it did not prevent me nor restrain me. Al-Hutay'ah said:

"Convey to the nobles of Banu Sa'd, with the utmost effort of the message, without shortfall or lie."

(p-105) ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ ﴿ياأيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَرْفَعُوا أصْواتَكم فَوْقَ صَوْتِ النَّبِيِّ ولا تَجْهَرُوا لَهُ بِالقَوْلِ كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكم لِبَعْضٍ أنْ تَحْبَطَ أعْمالُكم وأنْتُمْ لا تَشْعُرُونَ﴾ ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أصْواتَهم عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ امْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهم لِلتَّقْوى لَهم مَغْفِرَةٌ وأجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يُنادُونَكَ مِن وراءِ الحُجُراتِ أكْثَرُهم لا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ ﴿ولَوْ أنَّهم صَبَرُوا حَتّى تَخْرُجَ إلَيْهِمْ لَكانَ خَيْرًا لَهم واللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ ﴿ياأيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إنْ جاءَكم فاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوا أنْ تُصِيبُوا قَوْمًا بِجَهالَةٍ فَتُصْبِحُوا عَلى ما فَعَلْتُمْ نادِمِينَ﴾ [الحجرات: 6] ﴿واعْلَمُوا أنَّ فِيكم رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لَوْ يُطِيعُكم في كَثِيرٍ مِنَ الأمْرِ لَعَنِتُّمْ ولَكِنَّ اللَّهَ حَبَّبَ إلَيْكُمُ الإيمانَ وزَيَّنَهُ في قُلُوبِكم وكَرَّهَ إلَيْكُمُ الكُفْرَ والفُسُوقَ والعِصْيانَ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الرّاشِدُونَ﴾ [الحجرات: 7] ﴿فَضْلًا مِنَ اللَّهِ ونِعْمَةً واللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ [الحجرات: 8].

This surah is Medinan. Its connection with what precedes it is evident, because He mentioned the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions, then said: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [48:29]. So perhaps some of the believers who do righteous deeds did something that ought to be forbidden, and so the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, do not put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾.

It was the custom of the Arabs, and it remains so to this day, to share opinions, for each to speak as he wishes and do what he loves. Some of those who had not trained themselves in the etiquette of the Sharia did some of this. Qatadah said: "Some people would say: it should be such-and-such if such-and-such were revealed." Al-Hasan said: "A people slaughtered sacrifices before the Prophet (ﷺ), and a people did something on their own opinion during one of his campaigns, so this verse was revealed forbidding all of that." Ibn 'Abbas said: "They were forbidden to speak before his speech." The Arabs say: "I went ahead (taqaddamtu) in such-and-such," and "I put forward (qaddamtu) in it" when I spoke about it.

The majority read ﴿لا تُقَدِّمُوا﴾ (do not put forward). It is possible that it is transitive, and its object was omitted so that it would encompass everything that comes to mind of what is put forward, not aiming at a specific thing. The prohibition relates to the act itself without specifying a particular object, like their saying: "So-and-so gives and withholds." It is also possible that it is intransitive, in the sense of taqaddama (to advance), as you say: "wajh" in the sense of "tawajjaha" (to head toward), and the omitted element would be something reached by a preposition, meaning: do not advance in any matter whatsoever, or in what they love. This interpretation is supported by the reading of Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Haywah, al-Dahhak, Ya'qub and Ibn Miqsam: ﴿لا تَقَدَّمُوا﴾ with fatah on the ta', qaf and dal, indicating intransitivity, and the ta' was dropped for lightness, since the original is "la tatqaddamu."

Some of the Meccan readers read: "taqaddamu" with shaddah on the ta', the ta' of the present tense assimilated into the following ta', like the reading of al-Bazzi. It was also read: ﴿لا تَقْدِمُوا﴾, the present tense of qadima with kasr on the dal, from al-qudum (arrival), meaning: do not come forward to a matter of the affairs of religion before its arrival, and do not hasten regarding it.

Al-makan al-musamit wajh ar-rajul (the place facing a man's face) means near him. It has been said: in the phrase "bayna yadayi" (before me) with respect to the one sitting before whom, there is a broadening, as it encompasses the two directions of right and left. In His words ﴿بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ﴾ (before Allah), it is a metaphor of a metaphor of the figurative representation. The purpose of depicting the vileness and ugliness in it: they were forbidden from advancing into a matter without being guided by the models of the Book and the Sunnah. The meaning is: do not decide any matter except after they (Allah and His Messenger) have ruled on it and permitted it, so that you act by the revelation sent down, or follow the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This, and on this rests the interpretation of Ibn 'Abbas. Mujahid said: "Do not invent anything against Allah until Allah relates it through the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ)." In this prohibition there is a preparation for what comes after it: their being forbidden to raise their voices. When He forbade, He commanded taqwa, because part of taqwa is avoiding what is forbidden.

﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ﴾ (Indeed Allah is All-Hearing) of your words, ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ (All-Knowing) of your intentions and your deeds.

Then He called them a second time, to stir what He casts to them, to emphasize the improbability of the rulings that keep arising, and to make them attentive to listening. It was revealed because of the custom of the Bedouins of harshness and raising the voice.

﴿لا تَرْفَعُوا أصْواتَكُمْ﴾ means: when he speaks and you speak, (p-106) ﴿ولا تَجْهَرُوا لَهُ بِالقَوْلِ﴾ (nor speak loudly to him in speech) when you address him, because the rank of prophethood and messengership must be honored and glorified, and speech with the Messenger (ﷺ) should not be like speech with others. When it was revealed, Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "O Messenger of Allah, I will not speak to you except in a whisper, or like one who whispers, until I meet Allah." "It is narrated from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) that he would speak to the Prophet (ﷺ) like one who whispers, not making him hear until he asked him to repeat." Whenever Abu Bakr came before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)... [the text here reads: "وكانَ أبُو بَكْرٍ إذا قَدِمَ عَلى الرَّسُولِ ﷺ، قَوْمٌ أرْسَلَ إلَيْهِمْ مَن يُعَلِّمُهم كَيْفَ يُسْلِمُونَ"]

Whenever Abu Bakr came before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a people, he sent to them someone who would teach them how to embrace Islam, and he commanded them to tranquility and dignity in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Raising the voice and loudness were nothing but what was in their natures, not that it was intended by that to show contempt or arrogance, for that would have made their action disbelief, and the addressees were believers.

﴿كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكم لِبَعْضٍ﴾ (like the loudness of some of you to others): meaning in lack of concern and little respect. They were only forbidden from a specific kind of loudness. The scholars disliked raising the voice at the grave of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in the presence of a scholar, and in the mosques.

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: it was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who had a deafness in his ear and was loud of voice. His cutting himself off in his house for days because of this is well known, and he said: "O Messenger of Allah, when it was revealed, I feared that my deeds would be nullified." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Indeed you are among the people of Paradise." He also said to him once: "Are you not pleased to live praiseworthy and die a martyr?" He lived thus, then he was killed at al-Yamamah, on the day of Musaylimah, may Allah be pleased with him.

﴿أنْ تَحْبَطَ أعْمالُكُمْ﴾ (lest your deeds be nullified): if the verse is directed at one who raises his voice out of contempt, then that is disbelief, by which the deed is truly nullified. If it is addressed to the believer who does that out of heedlessness and following his habit, then what is nullified is only the righteousness of honoring the Prophet (ﷺ) and lowering the voice in his presence, had he done that. It is as if He said: lest the deeds that you were prepared to do, so that you would be rewarded for them, be nullified. "Lest be nullified" (an tahbata) is an object of purpose, and the governing element is "wa la tajharu" according to the Basran school of preference, and "wa la tarfa'u" according to the Kufan school of preference. Nevertheless, in terms of meaning, the nullification of the deed is a cause in both raising and loudness. 'Abdullah and Zayd ibn 'Ali read: ﴿فَتَحْبَطَ﴾ with the fa', which is a consequence of what precedes it.

﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أصْواتَهُمْ﴾ (Indeed those who lower their voices): it was said: it was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), because of what came from them of lowering the voice and of reaching the point of speaking to him like one who whispers.
